text: Selecting the right antibiotic starts with confirming the disease is actually bacterial — antibiotics cannot help against viral, parasitic, or nutritional-deficiency disease. Identifying the specific bacteria matters too: for example, coughing in fattening pigs treated with Amoxicillin may improve briefly (it's effective against Pasteurella) but relapse, because Pasteurella is often a secondary infection following damage from Mycoplasma, a bacterium with no cell wall that Amoxicillin (and the whole Betalactamine family) cannot touch — an antibiotic effective against both, like Tetracycline or Florfenicol, is more successful. Secondary infections are also common with viral disease: a virus-sick animal is weak, eats/drinks little, and this opens the door for bacteria — e.g. pigs with CSF often develop Salmonella-caused diarrhea and Pasteurella-caused coughing after a few days, so broad-spectrum antibiotics like TMP+Sulfa are recommended to limit secondary infection.
